# Agent C: self managed VM isolation with durable application recovery

Prepared independently on 2026-10-07. Status: candidate for challenge, not an adopted deployment or demonstrated production guarantee. No other discovery agent's conclusions were read. No experiment, infrastructure start, installation, image operation, credential inspection or external contact was performed.

## Recommendation and decisive limitation

Evaluate a Kubernetes managed Kata sandbox lane, with independently retained conversation state and a protected CephFS workspace, using cold replacement through the existing Claude SDK recovery path. Choose VM isolation to separate the engine and effect execution from the host and from one another. Do not make a suspended guest or a VM memory snapshot the authority for recovery. The application is greenfield. Existing library modules and fixtures are dependencies and measured constraints, not a deployed application's topology.

This candidate preserves the mandatory application -> governed runner -> Claude Agent SDK -> Claude Code path. It preserves accepted segment commit before external effect Activities, the exact original pending call and result, ambiguous Bash parking, authoritative cleanup before replacement, and unsupported child recovery denial. It introduces an infrastructure backend for the existing supervisor, not a second model executor.

The hardest unresolved requirement is positive knowledge that the previous execution has ceased. Kubernetes object deletion, lease expiry, Temporal timeout and a failed health check cannot establish that. On a partition, the candidate parks until an independent infrastructure operator proves termination and storage fencing. A fleet that cannot obtain that receipt does not offer automatic continuation across host unreachability. Safe parking is a supported outcome, and is materially different from transparent failover.

The strongest counterargument is that Kata, Kubernetes, Ceph and the fencing procedure add four operational systems without solving the application state protocol. A simpler dedicated VM or the existing container lane could be safer to operate if hostile code isolation is not required. This candidate is worth qualifying when the Security owner requires a separate guest kernel for untrusted effects and an existing team can operate the cluster and replicated filesystem. It is not justified solely by a desire to recover a long running agent.

## Governing record and current proof boundary

The starting authority is [the current checkpoint](../../canonical-documents.md#phase-1-independent-verification-checkpoint-2026-10-07), followed by canonical spec, plan, evidence and work items. The current [continue disposition](../../../../../../Workspace/ai-integrations-durability/python/claude_agent_sdk/docs/skill-recovery/evidence.md#approved-phase-1-continue-decision-2026-10-07) applies; earlier pending paragraphs are historical. DSR-0.6 remains an owner decision, not an implementation task already authorized. DSR-0.7 has no assigned gateway owner. DSR-0.4 is not a Phase 1 prerequisite.

The retained selected SDK 0.2.162 / CLI 2.1.274 proof is serial original pending recovery on the measured lane. The minimum SDK 0.2.153 / CLI 2.1.273 startup refusal is an approved failure disposition, not successful recovery. Synthetic result resume remains DEFECT. The Phase 1 evidence supplies no general cross host storage, spontaneous process loss, distributed ownership, production signing, full application composition or cold restart conformance. The strict JSON correction narrowed a proof fixture; it did not repeat a live qualification. No old source bound command is reused.

Current source anchors include `_runner.py:87` for the held SDK stream entry, `_runner.py:442` for conditional recovery append, `_runner.py:697` for copied session state, `_runner.py:707` for checkpoint readback, `host_session.py:188` for local ownership, `host_session.py:381` for teardown, `write_recovery.py:729` for original pending recovery, and `write_recovery.py:930` for effect placement in the reference proof. The HostSession docstring expressly excludes distributed lease and production supervisor claims. Source hashes and exact baseline are in the ledger. These fixtures must be adapted and qualified rather than silently reclassified as a production application.

## Components, exact research pins and maturity

These are proposed qualification pins, not installed binaries or a compatible bill of materials. Image digests, host kernel, firmware/microcode, CNI, CSI sidecars and runtime configuration must be bound before any deployment test. No distribution upgrade is proposed or authorized.

| Component | Proposed pin or observed current version | Status and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude recovery lane | SDK 0.2.162, CLI 2.1.274, Linux/Python 3.13; source plus dirty tree recorded in ledger | Demonstrated only within retained Phase 1 boundaries. Experimental recovery capability must pass admission. Published package metadata still classifies the plugin Alpha. |
| Temporal Python SDK | Repository requires >=1.33.0,<2; a deployment lock must select an exact build | Owner decision. A dependency range is not a production pin. Temporal service target, namespace, codec and retention are also owner decisions. |
| Kata Containers | 4.2.0, tag commit c7351e797efff8bfc6bd73da0eb1909be12e2cfe, released 2026-09-15 | Released OCI/CRI runtime with shim v2 architecture; cross component qualification here is untested. [Release](https://github.com/kata-containers/kata-containers/releases/tag/4.2.0). |
| Hypervisor and guest assets | Kata 4.2.0 QEMU 11.0.1, guest kernel 6.18.35, x86_64 Ubuntu resolute guest assets | Documented build inputs, not the digest of a tested artifact. Choose ordinary kata-qemu, without GPU or confidential computing variants. [Pinned versions](https://github.com/kata-containers/kata-containers/blob/4.2.0/versions.yaml). |
| containerd | Qualification candidate 2.3.0, released 2026-04-30; current latest 2.4.1, released 2026-09-24 | Kata's pinned versions file names the 2.3 lane. Select a patched exact 2.3 artifact at qualification after owner review; 2.3.0 is a research reproducibility pin, not a security recommendation to deploy an old patch. Latest 2.4.1 is not presumed compatible. [2.3.0 release](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.3.0), [2.4.1 release](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.4.1). |
| Kubernetes | 1.36.5, released 2026-09-23; observed latest 1.37.1 | Proposed maintained orchestration layer, using RuntimeClass and immutable Pod identities. 1.36 is in the CSI tested matrix; 1.37 is not. [1.36.5](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/releases/tag/v1.36.5), [1.37.1](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/releases/tag/v1.37.1). |
| CephFS | Tentacle 20.2.4, released 2026-08-19, tag commit 7f793731f1b39eb4f465e960113d2363c311b964 | Candidate replicated filesystem; exact guest/virtio-fs/client atomic create and persistence conformance untested. Official release schedule marks target EOL 2027-06-01; this is a published schedule, not a guarantee of future support. [Release schedule](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/blob/main/doc/releases/releases.yml). |
| Ceph CSI | 3.18.1, released 2026-10-01 | Project labels itself GA; CephFS file RWX provisioning GA. Tested Kubernetes versions are 1.34,1.35,1.36; Arm64 is experimental. Select x86_64. No RWOP or volume group snapshot dependency is used. [Pinned support matrix](https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/blob/v3.18.1/README.md). |
| Firecracker alternative | Current 1.17.0, released 2026-09-10 | Maintained microVMM alternative, not selected for this initial lane. Kata 4.2.0's own Firecracker pin is 1.12.1, so pairing Kata with newest Firecracker is unqualified. [Release](https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/releases/tag/v1.17.0). |

Kata documents one VM per Pod sandbox, a host shim/runtime, a guest agent and a hypervisor. Several containers within the same Pod share that VM. Therefore placing hostile Bash beside the trusted segment Worker in one Pod would defeat the intended separate guest boundary. The documented lifecycle is useful precedent, but API success still needs a host termination oracle in this deployment. [Pinned architecture](https://github.com/kata-containers/kata-containers/blob/4.2.0/docs/design/architecture/README.md).

## Complete candidate architecture

Capability labels apply narrowly: vendor runtime/storage descriptions are documented; retained Phase 1 observations are demonstrated within their recorded lane; the complete composition is inferred and untested; missing independent fence, key owner and retention values are owner decisions; timeout-only takeover, arbitrary exactly-once Bash and recovery after loss of all acknowledged authorities are unsupported. A documented component does not make the composition demonstrated.

1. A new application authored Temporal Workflow holds orchestration state, accepted segment identity, pending decisions and exact recorded outcomes. The application registers its own signed handlers/validators and explicit Worker Versioning behavior. Queue names are new application configuration. The fixture's queue names are not inferred deployment facts. Workflow code never launches or inspects operating system processes.
2. Trusted Workflow Workers run outside untrusted effect sandboxes. Segment Activity Workers run the existing SDK controller/runner inside one Kata Pod per owned segment attempt. The supervisor backend creates that Pod using the existing lifecycle interface, with namespace/lineage/attempt identity labels and digest pinned images. The engine may contact the approved provider; its egress and token budgets remain separately governed. Native shell stays disabled and package/read confinement stays in both decision routes.
3. Every effect Activity obtains its own distinct Kata sandbox. It receives only the admitted package subset read only and the lineage `work/` directory writable, at the canonical absolute path. It receives neither the session store nor protected claims/ownership metadata, Worker launch credentials, Kubernetes service account token, provider credential, or the supervisor socket. Effect network egress is disabled for the initial local filesystem/Bash contract. Adding external network destinations is a separate policy decision and test scope. A trusted Activity wrapper creates the claim before it launches Bash. The untrusted child does not perform claim admission.
4. CephFS provides the same absolute lineage workspace path to every permitted Worker. Protected directories hold package snapshots, claims and supervisor ownership records; untrusted mounts expose only `work/`. Host UID/GID mappings, no symlink escape, separate storage credentials and immutable package digests are mandatory. A read only package mount does not protect another writable alias: the test rig must inventory all guest and host mount aliases.
5. The production SessionStore adapter stores immutable transcript entries with UUID deduplication and a conditional expected head, plus a manifest binding session ID, checkpoint UUID, transcript prefix digest and original pending request. It uses protected CephFS state, immutable entry objects and a serialized head update with tested fsync/rename/error behavior. It must fail closed on conflicting duplicate UUID, lost write acknowledgment, stale prefix and mixed manifest. This adapter is required new integration; the local experiment SQLite/conditional append fixture is not its proof. An append acknowledgment is emitted only after the tested persistent storage acknowledgment and readback. No object store's eventual listing is used for admission.
6. One ownership record per namespace and lineage serializes attempt admission outside the guest. Its immutable acquisition record binds host boot ID, runtime sandbox UID, VMM PID/start identity, runner identity and workspace identity. The trusted supervisor is its only writer. The implementation must use a tested atomic filesystem admission primitive, retain an unresolved record after coordinator death, and never reclaim it solely because a TTL expired. Distributed admission is a new backend of the existing supervisor contract, not an SDK lease. Two independent application histories targeting the same lineage still contend here.
7. A reachable host teardown collects guest task exit, sandbox exit, shim/VMM exit, host process identity inventory and runtime resource absence. It then revokes storage/egress access as needed and persists a cleanup receipt. The Workflow accepts that receipt before replacement admission. For an unreachable host, the operator must use an independent power or infrastructure fence with durable evidence that the host cannot execute, plus Ceph client eviction/blocklisting with the relevant OSD epoch barrier. Deleting a Pod object is insufficient. The candidate defaults to PARK when either receipt is unavailable. The actual BMC/provider fence mechanism is an owner decision and must be pinned before host partition qualification.
8. The signed decision gateway is a separate trusted service. It is the sole authorized approval/answer/resume Update caller, verifies request identity at the existing contract boundary and retains Update ID and final result for client retry. Signing keys and codec keys are never mounted into effect or segment guests. Key release uses the approved secrets system. Ordinary Kata isolation is not remote attestation or confidential computing; a deployment that requires either needs another owner decision and hardware qualification.
9. An external janitor consults Temporal namespace/run/lineage status and protected identity records. It retains live, idle and parked state regardless of mtime, including unresolved claims. It does not release a claim or expire ownership as a cleanup shortcut. Closed work/package cleanup and claim/history/session retention must be coordinated with Reset and Continue-As-New windows. Retention duration and capacity are explicit owner decisions.

Temporal records history and accepted Activity results; it does not atomically commit an arbitrary Bash effect with its completion event. A physical success before durable completion therefore remains ambiguous, and Option R parks without a second spawn or model continuation. Regular effect Activities remain external to the accepted segment. [Official at least once explanation](https://temporal.io/blog/execution-guarantees).

## State ownership and persistence contract

All rows below are proposed requirements unless explicitly labeled demonstrated. A successful acknowledgment cannot mean only that a guest wrote into its page cache.

| State class | Owner and authoritative storage | Acknowledgment, consistency and identity | Retention and restore | Missing state behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Temporal history, accepted segment, decisions and outcomes | Application Workflow; chosen Temporal service persistence | Service history commit; namespace, Workflow ID, Run ID, lineage, accepted segment and Update identity. Queries/Search Attributes are discovery only. Replay reconstructs ordered accepted facts, not physical execution. | Namespace retention and closed handover histories must cover allowed Reset windows. Service recovery responsibility belongs to deployment owner. | Missing history is no authority to reuse files or execute. Stop and investigate. |
| Claude trajectory/checkpoint | Production SessionStore adapter; protected CephFS objects | Durable append and expected-head acknowledgment, readback, UUID/digest/prefix equality, exact pending call/result typed JSON identity. Local trajectory not accepted by itself. | Keep all required checkpoint prefixes through active wait/park and allowed replay. Restore to exact accepted checkpoint only, never sanitized exports or reconstructed text. | No new session fallback. Park/refuse before SDK startup. |
| Package/policy/runtime | Build and deployment owner; immutable package object plus retained admission manifest | Package snapshot digest, exact Skill names, policy digest, SDK/CLI/image/hook hashes and Worker Deployment Version. Verify at each segment and before claims. | Retain versions needed by open/pinned histories. No silent upgrade or engine self update. | Refuse mismatch and route to explicit migration/drain decision. |
| Mutable generated files | Harness workspace service; CephFS `work/` | Native semantics plus tested persistent acknowledgments. Write/Edit guards bind relevant pre/post images, serialized conflicting access and generation. A manifest generation alone is not a transaction over later writes. | Storage replication addresses a lost compute disk; authorized restore must carry restore identity and be coordinated with claims/outcomes. | Park on missing, inconsistent or unverified restored workspace. Do not infer safety from an empty directory. |
| Protected claims | Trusted effect wrapper; separate protected CephFS directory | Cross host O_CREAT/O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW with tested persistence before Bash start, stable lineage/key/ordinal/digest. First failed or unknown postclaim attempt never releases claim. No dropped high-water counter is reintroduced. | Never roll back independently of workspace/outcome state. Retain until approved history/reset window closes. | Existing/missing/unverifiable claim integrity or attempt>1 parks. An undetected storage rollback can violate at most one spawn; this remains an explicit unsupported boundary until proven. |
| Execution ownership and cleanup | Existing supervisor with new infrastructure backend; protected journal and receipts accepted in history | Atomic admission; host boot/runtime/VMM/runner identities; actual zero owned execution plus storage fence. Timeout/lease is an observation, not termination. Cleanup receipt precedes ownership transfer. | Unresolved ownership survives control process crash, storage outage and coordinator restart. Never TTL-reclaim. | Park when old host cannot be checked or fenced. Do not replace from missing journal. |
| Keys, authentication and optional attestation | Security and gateway owners; their approved key/secrets systems | Version/key ID, authorized caller, canonical digest, per decision/park identity, expiry and minimum token version. Credential availability does not authorize execution. | Retain verification/codec keys for retained histories; rotate under explicit compatibility policy. No guest memory snapshot retains authoritative approval state. | Fail closed; human wait expires under stated no answer rule. No attestation claim for ordinary Kata. |

CephFS documents multiclient consistency but explicitly relaxes some POSIX behavior and describes writeback error reporting. These documents are reasons to test the exact path through CSI, host client, virtio-fs and guest, not proof that every filesystem operation needed by the application is correct. [Pinned POSIX differences](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/blob/v20.2.4/doc/cephfs/posix.rst).

Ceph client eviction can fence storage access and lose unflushed data. Blocklist propagation uses an OSD map epoch barrier. Storage fencing cannot stop an old model request or arbitrary external socket, so the stronger execution cleanup requirement remains. Never un-blocklist an old client as an automated restore step. [Pinned eviction mechanism](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/blob/v20.2.4/doc/cephfs/eviction.rst).

## Cold restart versus VM snapshot restore

Cold replacement bootstraps new guest assets, verifies ownership/cleanup and retained state, then invokes the original pending recovery adapter through the mandatory SDK entrypoint. Lost TCP/vsock connections, SDK task identity and guest processes are not expected to survive. An accepted question during the outage is replayed from Workflow state and applied once to its original pending call, after cleanup and exact identity validation.

Firecracker full snapshots capture guest memory and emulated device state; disks are separately managed by the integrator. Memory backing remains needed during resumed execution. Snapshot files require external authentication/security, and vsock connections reset while network survival is not guaranteed. Diff snapshots remain developer preview in 1.17.0. Host fsync is not an off host replica acknowledgment. These facts make snapshots useful for a boot optimization experiment, not a substitute for the application state protocol. [Pinned snapshot contract](https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/v1.17.0/docs/snapshotting/snapshot-support.md).

Reject restoring a running Claude guest snapshot as initial recovery: it can revive old credentials, in-flight requests, claim-adjacent state and the previous owner. If later considered, restore into an isolated no-egress/no-effect quarantine, establish unique VM identity, validate all durable state and ownership, discard stale transport and cross the same admission gate. No memory continuity guarantee is claimed. A boot template with no live session, no keys and no lineage state is a different, optional latency optimization. It still needs compatibility and isolation proof.

## Fault coverage and outcomes

The following are falsifiable requirements, not observed results. A retry is permitted only for a demonstrably effect-free segment or a supported repeatable effect under its native guard. Bash is never respawned after an uncertain claim boundary.

| Fault | Expected behavior | Required oracle and limitation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SDK/Worker process crash | Stop owned sandbox; cold recover the last accepted checkpoint, or park uncertain claimed effect. | Actual owned PID/start inventory, preserved prefix, effect count; controlled kill does not establish arbitrary spontaneous loss proof. |
| Container destroy | Treat guest task loss separately from sandbox/VMM lifecycle; verify full sandbox termination before replacement. | Runtime UID, guest task absence, shim/VMM exit and host resource inventory. API object absence alone fails the test. |
| Guest kernel panic or hang | Host supervisor terminates the matching VMM and persists cleanup; cold recovery or Bash park. | Guest fault evidence plus host VMM exit receipt; no cooperative guest cleanup assumption. |
| Host unreachable with process still alive | Park, even if Temporal schedules another attempt. Continue only after independent host termination and storage fencing. | Observer sees old process heartbeat or delayed external requests; replacement startup count must remain zero until receipts. |
| Permanent compute host and local disk loss | Recover only from independently acknowledged replicated state, after credible host-dead receipt. | Delete/loss of compute disk while independent storage remains, compare acknowledged object hashes; co-located storage cannot pass this topology. |
| Replicated storage/quorum unavailable | No checkpoint/claim acknowledgment, no new effect or replacement; retain uncertain admission. | Inject read/write/fsync failures and hung I/O; attempt inventory shows zero post-refusal effects. |
| Stale or partial storage restore | Refuse mismatched prefix/generation/identity; if a coordinated midrun rollback cannot be detected, report FAIL/unsupported rather than pass. | Restore claim directory, work tree and session objects independently, including same manifest generation. A complete matching rollback is not inherently detectable by this design. |
| Simultaneous replacements/reset branches | One supervisor admission; losers refuse before SDK startup. | Two host contenders with same namespace/lineage; SDK/model start count one, claim winner count one. Atomic transcript append alone is insufficient. |
| Effect succeeds before durable result | Ambiguous Bash parks, preserves claim, does not send an unknown result to model, and does not re-execute. | Independent append-only physical witness records one invocation; no later model request. File existence alone cannot distinguish repeated overwrite. |
| Cancellation with detached descendants | Cancellation enters stop state; host destroys sandbox/VMM, retains uncertain claim; no replacement until cleanup. | Child deliberately double-forks/setsid and writes witness after parent exit. Guest process groups are not the containment oracle. |
| Engine/package/policy changes during wait | Refuse changed contract before claims/model start; keep old pinned lane or explicit migration decision. | Replace each hash/version separately and trace admission order; do not interpret as a model tool error. |
| Approval accepted while host fails | Accepted signed Update remains durable; no duplicate application; answer only original pending request after cleanup. | History Update identity/result, pending record, exact recovery argument JSON and model transport counter. Client timeout is not assumed rejection. |
| Retention while idle or parked | Janitor keeps trajectory/workspace/claims/ownership even if old mtimes or no active guest. | Run janitor with live/park/closed/resettable cases; deletion witness shows only eligible closed state. |
| Temporal service unavailable | Existing owned processes may still run; supervisor budgets/stop policy apply locally. No external effects based on an unaccepted segment. | Deny history completion acknowledgment and show no effect dispatch; cluster outage does not terminate processes automatically. |

Kubernetes itself warns that force deletion does not confirm process termination and can leave duplicate processes using the same storage/identity. This candidate therefore forbids treating forced deletion as its authoritative cleanup receipt. [Official force deletion guidance](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/force-delete-stateful-set-pod/).

## Testable qualification protocol

Use the existing SDK controller, runner, host supervisor and `sdk_shutdown_probe.py` inventory. Add fault barriers and an infrastructure backend to those seams only after separate implementation authorization. Do not create a new executor. The tests use a deterministic scripted model transport first; they never claim that scripted transport qualifies a real model or installed-source provenance.

Topology T0 is the retained isolated image `sha256:cf99136b343499bf8762afe546e24bf728c8db00ceee3931b6dc629275498afa`, existing supervisor and source-bound offline controls. Existing completed tests are evidence to reuse, not rerun. New read-only admission/state mismatch controls can be prepared offline with no credentials. Topology T1 is an authorized two compute host Kata cluster, separate Ceph failure domains and a separate observer/Temporal service. It binds every component above, image digests, guest/host kernel, UID/GID, runtime configuration, CSI/CNI, filesystem ID, namespace, lineage, mount identity and version. T2 adds independent host power fencing and controlled compute disk destruction. T3 adds disposable storage restore/partition fault control. T1/T2/T3 do not exist as demonstrated facilities in this record and require infrastructure permission before setup or execution.

Each test records the input manifest, source hash, exact injection barrier and acknowledgment receipt, full unnormalized SDK/probe observations, history, transcript prefix/object hashes, accepted call/result, protected claim bytes, host/runtime identities, cleanup receipts and an independent physical witness. Keep the raw archive; sanitized publication is separate. Negative controls must intentionally weaken the tested gate in an isolated copy and fail the intended oracle. No test accepts its own mock cleanup callback as proof of actual shutdown.

| Test family and barrier pair | Topology, concrete injection | Expected continuation/park and duplicate oracle | Cleanup prerequisites, authorization and limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C-01 Before/after session append acknowledgment | T1: kill segment guest or host after bytes exist but before durable ack, then after ack; delay head update and inject conflicting UUID append. | Unacknowledged trajectory cannot advance accepted checkpoint. Acknowledged exact prefix survives cold replacement; conflicting UUID refuses. Compare independent storage readback and SDK input prefix. | Old sandbox stopped before readback/recovery; T1 permission. T0 may test adapter refusal with scripted data only. |
| C-02 Before/after accepted segment commit | T1: cut Activity completion response and Workflow Task commit independently after exact tool_deferred. | No external effect before accepted commit. After commit, the exact recorded call is dispatched once; repeat completion does not mint a second ordinal/key. Witness and ordered history identify duplicates. | Positive cleanup receipt before replacement; T1 permission. Accepted client output is not history commit proof. |
| C-03 Before/after claim creation/persistence ack | T1/T3: kill wrapper around exclusive create, inject fsync errors, race two hosts and symlink replacement. | No Bash without durable claim. After claim uncertainty, park even if no visible physical effect. At most one successful creator and one spawn; missing claim integrity blocks. | Stop both contender sandboxes and retain claims; T1/T3 permission. Guest filesystem semantics alone are insufficient. |
| C-04 Before/after effect start | T1: barrier immediately before exec and immediately after child entry witness; kill wrapper/VMM. | Preclaim safe refusal has zero spawns. Any uncertain postclaim state parks; postentry witness count one and no later spawn. | Full VMM cleanup required; T1 permission. PID observation alone can miss very short effects. |
| C-05 Before/after physical effect completion | T1: Bash appends unique key to separate observer witness, writes work file, exits; lose completion observation on either side. | Known result returned only if definitive outcome retained under original identity; otherwise park, never infer from work file. Witness count stays one. | Effect sandbox shutdown receipt; T1 permission. Observer service is test evidence, not a new keyed production effect API. |
| C-06 Before/after durable outcome commit | T1: lose worker before result acknowledgment and after ActivityTaskCompleted history event. | Before durable result ambiguous Bash parks; after recorded definitive result reuse exact content/is_error with no effect re-execution. Repeatable file effects separately prove postimage/overlap rules. | Existing effect owner cleanup plus retained result; T1 permission. Actual filesystem/Bash native semantics require native tests. |
| C-07 Before/after original pending recovery | T1: fail after admission but before recovery callback, then after result append but before next model turn; duplicate result or Boolean/numeric identity substitution. | Recover only exact original call/result. No synthetic alternate path, no changed answer, no duplicate turn from competing owner. Use UUID/head and transport counters. | Old and interrupted replacement receipts before next admission; T1 permission. Later bounded real model run requires separate exact approval and allowance. |
| C-08 Before/after ownership transfer | T1/T2: supervisor dies before persisting cleanup, after cleanup, before acquisition and after acquisition; contender on second host; host partition with live VMM. | Unresolved old ownership parks. Recorded cleanup permits exactly one new owner. Lost acquisition reply reconciles same identity rather than creates another sandbox. Model/effect witness detects any overlap. | Independent host fence and Ceph epoch evidence for T2; extra permission. Lease expiry must not make the test pass. |
| C-09 Decision/cancellation ordering | T1: accepted signed Update during partition, client response lost, then replay same Update ID; cancellation before/after acceptance and result application. | Deterministic cancellation precedence; accepted unapplied action retained, applied once to original question when eligible. Duplicate/stale park/expiry/key-version tokens refuse. | Stop old guest before answer delivery; gateway implementation authorization and T1 permission. T0 can prepare token/identity inputs, not prove authenticated gateway enforcement. |
| C-10 Restore and retention corruption | T3: remove trajectory object, restore claims alone, restore work alone, restore all to same older generation, wrong namespace/reused Workflow ID; janitor against idle/parked and closed lineage. | Detectable mismatches refuse before model/effect. Complete unsignaled matching rollback is a falsification candidate, not an assumed pass. Live/parked state remains. | All relevant guests stopped before restore; storage operator permission. If missing postclaim evidence permits spawn, candidate fails supported at-most-one boundary. |
| C-11 Containment and changed policy | T1: actual Bash double-fork, attempt supervisor/claims/package/credential mount access; suppressed decision hook; change admitted package or engine while waiting. | Zero forbidden reads/writes, no surviving child after VMM stop, policy fault before model/effect. Read/Glob/Grep positives and exact Skill positives remain admitted. | Test host inventory plus guest inventory; T1 permission. Reuse Phase 1 backstop evidence; run only new deployment escape surfaces. |

For each barrier pair repeat independently for process kill, container destruction and guest failure; use T2 for host loss and T3 for storage partitions. This is a cross product planned qualification, not a set of already passed cases. Run independent before/after cases with fresh output and lineage IDs. Pin a nonfinite/malformed JSON negative, changed original pending identity, duplicate head and withheld cleanup control. Every failed cleanup stops the series. No provider spending is involved in scripted qualification. Native/real provider proof needs separately approved commands and reactive allowance or final preventive gate as applicable.

## Prior art disposition and operational burden

| Prior art | Reuse/reference/reject | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing controller/runner/HostSession/probe/original recovery fixtures | Reuse and adapt infrastructure backend | Keeps one SDK entrypoint and measured ordering; local SQLite/Docker ownership is not distributed proof. |
| Kata 4.2.0 shim v2 / RuntimeClass / guest lifecycle | Reuse maintained orchestration integration | Provides a guest kernel boundary and standard Pod lifecycle. Separate effect Pod required. |
| CephFS + Ceph CSI | Reference and qualify | Matches the proposed shared POSIX class and managed lifecycle. Exact atomic create, durable acknowledgment, host/guest cache and rollback boundary still need tests. |
| Temporal regular Activities and history | Reuse | Already the orchestration/effect outcome seam; retries do not atomically undo or deduplicate external effects. |
| Firecracker 1.17.0 full snapshot API | Reference; reject as active session durability authority | Useful VM mechanism, but external disks, transport, identity and claims still need an application protocol. |
| firecracker-containerd | Reject for initial qualification, not abandoned | Repository is not archived; observed default branch last commit be68640a5d2237f5b427c37c1f5809ec154126c5 on 2026-07-16 and repository push metadata 2026-09-25. No latest release API entry. README requires a specialized containerd build and describes CRI compatibility as roadmap. Maintenance activity is not a supported compatibility release. [Pinned README](https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker-containerd/blob/be68640a5d2237f5b427c37c1f5809ec154126c5/README.md). |
| Kata newest Firecracker or Cloud Hypervisor substitution | Reject without separate compatibility qualification | Kata's own pinned build inputs differ from latest vendor releases. |
| Kubernetes forced replacement / CSI detach / TTL lease | Reject as sole ownership proof | API deletion and volume status do not prove old guest death or external request cessation. |

Required new integration comprises the Kata backend for the existing supervisor, protected distributed ownership admission and durable cleanup receipts, the production conditional SessionStore adapter, workspace preparation/mount policy and claim persistence qualification, the signed gateway/key/codec deployment, janitor identity/retention controls, and fault barriers in the existing rig. The existing effect implementation remains the only effect executor path. These are requirements for later authorized work, not a request to build them now.

Costs include KVM capable compute, separate effect guest memory/boot overhead, image and guest asset supply chain management, CSI/CNI and virtio-fs operations, independent Ceph metadata/data/quorum failure domains, backup and restore drills, fencing access and on-call ownership, retained transcripts/workspace/claims capacity, codec key retention, versioned Worker pools and fault qualification. No numeric product SLO or capacity target is invented. Measure concurrent active guests, idle/parked retained bytes, claim create/fsync latency, checkpoint append/restore latency and confirmed cleanup latency before sizing. Keeping no guest alive during human waits reduces compute demand but does not reduce retention obligations.

## Decision boundary for the lead synthesis

This candidate is complete enough to challenge and turn into testable deployment requirements. It is not complete enough to declare compatible production components or authorize Phase 2 implementation. The Security owner must choose the required isolation level, filesystem semantics and failure boundary. Deployment/storage owners must choose exact patched artifacts and digests, Ceph failure-domain placement, allowed rollback boundary, BMC/provider fencing and authoritative receipt format, production session and retention contract. The gateway owner and Temporal service/codec/versioning owners must be named.

Durable independent storage and an independent physical or provider fence are prerequisites owned by deployment and storage/security roles. Neither is available or demonstrated merely because the local isolated image exists. The smallest meaningful new deployment experiment is one scripted, original pending call on host A, an acknowledged checkpoint and claim on independent CephFS, then a control-plane partition while A remains observably alive. A contender on host B must refuse before SDK startup. After an independently evidenced host-A stop and Ceph epoch fence, B may recover the exact recorded result once with the physical witness unchanged. This jointly falsifies false cleanup, duplicate ownership and effect replay with one scenario; it does not qualify all storage rollback or kernel fault cases. It requires permission for two-host infrastructure and fencing, but no provider/model call. A mock fence can prepare refusal tests offline and cannot substitute for this experiment.

Do not claim autonomous failover from an unreachable host until independent termination and storage fencing pass T2. Do not claim recovery after total acknowledged storage loss. Do not claim detection of an unsignaled fully consistent midrun rollback merely because a manifest generation matches. If the chosen storage cannot deliver tested atomic exclusive creation, change the storage class or drop the conditional at-most-one-spawn claim under an explicit redesign decision; silently weakening the guard is not acceptable.

The single next action is to challenge this candidate's ownership, storage acknowledgment and restore boundaries against the other independent reports, then present DSR-0.6's concrete operator choice. No implementation is requested by this report.
